newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia launches satellite with monkeys, insects.
newsitem.headline: Russia launches satellite with monkeys, insects.

text.p: Russia launched a satellite on Tuesday carrying two monkeys, bugs, snails, flies and plants for a two-week space trip, a space official said.
A military space forces spokesman told Reuters the satellite Bion-11 was lifted into space by Soyuz-U rocket from the northern cosmodrome of Plesetsk, 600 km (400 miles) from Moscow.
"The launch was succesful," the spokesman said, adding the flight's cost was $30 million. "Half of this sum was financed by the U.S. space agency NASA," he said.
France, Ukraine and Lithuania were also involved in the project, the spokesman said.
The Bion, weigh 6,280 kg (13,840 lb), was lifted into a 290 km (180 mile) high orbit.
"The satellite's "crew' has not been specially prepared for this space trip and it will be very important to understand how weightlessness influences them," the spokesman said.
Bion's flight will produce new data which will be used for future manned space flights.
The spokesman said the satellite was scheduled to land in 14 days' time in southern Siberia.
"Animals, insects and plants will be tested after the flight and then will return to the zoo," the spokesman said.
The first Bion satellite was launched in the former Soviet Union in 1973.
